sentences.text: Shri B.S. Sahu - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Amit Bhurrak - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/Stat
 Shri Manoj Kumar Mishra - Advocate for the objector.

Order 
This is second application filed under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 r/w Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on behalf of applicant, who is in jail since 29.10.2023 in relation to FIR/Crime No.801/2023, registered at Police Station- Station Ganj, District Narsinghpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code.

The first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 29.04.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.12480/2024.
2.

Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submits that looking to the offence alleged against the present applicant and the period of conviction prescribed therein viz-a-vis period of custody i.e.
29.04.2024, the bail application can be considered and applicant can be released on bail.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that the present applicant has past criminal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17348 2 MCRC-12995-2025 antecedents and number of cases registered against him of similar nature.

He has further submitted that present applicant is the resident of Rajasthan and if bail is granted then there is every possibility that he would be absconding and trial would be delayed unnecessarily.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the objector has also supported the submission made by counsel for the State and prays for rejection of the application.

5. Considering the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary so also the period of sentenced prescribed under the respective sections, I am inclined to consider and allow this bail application.
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) subject to furnishing two local sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned.
7. On being released on bail, the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 480(3) of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Rao Shubhkaran vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159648485/
